title: Lesson 9. Tidy folders
description: Folders inside folders, renaming, moving and copying files

questions.prompt: Match the action with its meaning
Put the copying steps in order
After copying, the file is in both the old and new places.
Easiest way to move a file into a folder?
questions.explain: Press, hold, drag to the folder, release.

questions.prompt: Where does the cat picture go when tidying?
You can spot a picture by its icon — it looks like a picture.
questions.explain: A tip from the "Sort into drawers" quest.

questions.text: To change a file's name: right-click → ___ → Enter.

questions.prompt: What do we do with the empty "Mess" folder at the end?

learn.intro: A schoolbag has pockets — so does a folder! Today we tidy up like real pros.

slides.text: A schoolbag has pockets for notebooks, pens, food. A folder can have **smaller folders** too. We make: Texts, Pictures, Games.

check.prompt: You can make folders inside a folder.

slides.text: **Rename**: right-click the file → Rename → new name → Enter.
**Move**: drag the file into another folder with the mouse. Like moving a notebook to another pocket — it is no longer in the old place.

check.prompt: After moving, is the file still in the old place?
check.explain: Moving takes it away from the old place.

slides.text: **Copy**: right-click → Copy → go to another folder → right-click → **Paste**.
Copying is like a photocopy: the notebook stays, and an identical one appears in the new place.

check.prompt: How is copying different from moving?
check.explain: A copy is a photocopy; the original stays.
